_doc: TENTH HELD-OUT real project (Phase 5, learning-from-corrections measurement): cJSON v1.7.19 (samples/realworld/cJSON, upstream commit c859b25; ~5.3K lines of library C and headers (cJSON.c, cJSON.h, cJSON_Utils.c, cJSON_Utils.h, test.c) plus ~4.3K lines of the project's own unit tests; a JSON parser/printer library plus cJSON_Utils for JSON Pointer, JSON Patch and Merge Patch; the bundled Unity test framework, the fuzzing folder and the test data folders were removed). 10 behavioural (scenario) and 4 structural questions written from facts verified in the source BEFORE Verity was ever run on it. Every must_mention token was grepped verbatim (case-sensitive) in the tree, and the first token names the function where the behaviour is decided. Paraphrases and neighbours for the Phase 5 learning measurement are in bench/realworld_heldout10_followup.json.

cases.q: What happens when the input has thousands of arrays nested inside each other, like [[[[ ... ]]]]?
What happens when a value in the input starts with a minus sign but no digits follow it, as in [-]?
What happens when a string in the input has an opening quote but the closing quote never comes?
What happens when a string contains a \u escape for the first half of a UTF-16 surrogate pair, but the \u escape after it is not a valid second half?
What happens if memory runs out while the parser is creating the item for the next member of an object?
What happens when I print JSON into a buffer I allocated myself and the output turns out to be bigger than that buffer?
What happens when I tell the parser that nothing but whitespace may follow the JSON value, and there is extra text after it?
With the normal object key lookup, will looking up "Name" find a member that is stored as "name"?
What happens when a JSON Pointer path uses an array index with a leading zero, like /list/01?
What happens when a JSON Patch entry has a valid path but its "op" is something the library does not support, like "rename"?
Who calls the function that turns a quoted string in the input text into a C string?
Where can a program plug in its own malloc and free for the library to use, and where are they stored?
Which function writes the tab characters that indent each member of an object when pretty-printing?
Which function works out the list of operations that turns one JSON document into another, and which helper builds each operation entry?
